\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سيرة} \ar{ذاتية} (sīra dhātiyya)}{سيرة ذاتية (sīra dhātiyya)}]{\ar{سيرة} \ar{ذاتية} (sīra dhātiyya) — a CV; a life story}

\label{lesson:AR-C519-sira-dhatiyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an adviser, then the Arabic for to aspire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سيرة} \ar{ذاتية}}
\textbf{\ar{سيرة} \ar{ذاتية}} — \emph{sīra dhātiyya} — \textquotedblleft{}a CV; a life story\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أرسلت} \ar{سيرتي} \ar{الذاتية} \ar{إلى} \ar{الشركة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{arsaltu sīratī adh-dhātiyya ilā ash-sharika.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I sent my CV to the company.
\end{quote}

\ar{سيرة} alone is a life story, a biography.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سيرة} \ar{ذاتية}} (\emph{sīra dhātiyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-y-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to go, to travel\textquotedblright{} (Lane): a \emph{sīra} is a way of going, the path of a life. \emph{Dhātiyya} is \textquotedblleft{}of the self\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{dhāt}, self.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sīra dhātiyya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sīra dhātiyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arsaltu sīratī adh-dhātiyya ilā ash-sharika.} — I sent my CV to the company.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an adviser, then the Arabic for to aspire, then say \emph{sīra dhātiyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{سيرة} \ar{ذاتية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A CV; a life story\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تطوع} (taṭawwaʿa)}{تطوع (taṭawwaʿa)}]{\ar{تطوع} (taṭawwaʿa) — to volunteer}

\label{lesson:AR-C519-tatawwaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to aspire, then the Arabic for a CV.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تطوع}}
\textbf{\ar{تطوع}} — \emph{taṭawwaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to volunteer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تطوعت} \ar{أختي} \ar{في} \ar{المستشفى} \ar{في} \ar{الصيف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taṭawwaʿat ukhtī fī al-mustashfā fī aṣ-ṣayf.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister volunteered at the hospital in the summer.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتطوع}, \emph{yataṭawwaʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تطوع}} (\emph{taṭawwaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṭ-w-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to comply, to be willing\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives Form V taṭawwaʿa as to do a good thing that is not required.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṭawwaʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṭawwaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṭawwaʿat ukhtī fī al-mustashfā fī aṣ-ṣayf.} — My sister volunteered at the hospital in the summer.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to aspire, then the Arabic for a CV, then say \emph{taṭawwaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تطوع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To volunteer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تبرع} (tabarraʿa)}{تبرع (tabarraʿa)}]{\ar{تبرع} (tabarraʿa) — to donate}

\label{lesson:AR-C519-tabarraa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a CV, then the Arabic for to volunteer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تبرع}}
\textbf{\ar{تبرع}} — \emph{tabarraʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to donate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تبرع} \ar{أبي} \ar{بالمال} \ar{للمدرسة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tabarraʿa abī bi-l-māl li-l-madrasa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father donated money to the school.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتبرع}, \emph{yatabarraʿ}.

It takes \ar{بـ} for the gift: \ar{تبرع} \ar{بالدم}, to give blood.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تبرع}} (\emph{tabarraʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-r-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to excel, to surpass\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form V tabarraʿa is to give more than is asked: to give freely.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabarraʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabarraʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabarraʿa abī bi-l-māl li-l-madrasa.} — My father donated money to the school.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a CV, then the Arabic for to volunteer, then say \emph{tabarraʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تبرع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To donate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{متدرب} (mutadarrib)}{متدرب (mutadarrib)}]{\ar{متدرب} (mutadarrib) — a trainee, an intern}

\label{lesson:AR-C519-mutadarrib}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to volunteer, then the Arabic for to donate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{متدرب}}
\textbf{\ar{متدرب}} — \emph{mutadarrib} — \textquotedblleft{}a trainee, an intern\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يعمل} \ar{في} \ar{المكتب} \ar{ثلاثة} \ar{متدربين}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaʿmalu fī al-maktab thalāthat mutadarribīn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Three trainees work in the office.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{متدرب}} (\emph{mutadarrib}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-r-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to be used to, to be practised in\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Mutadarrib is the participle of Form V: one being trained.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to volunteer, then the Arabic for to donate, then say \emph{mutadarrib} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تدرب} (tadarraba)}{تدرب (tadarraba)}]{\ar{تدرب} (tadarraba) — to practise}

\label{lesson:AR-C519-tadarraba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to donate, then the Arabic for a trainee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تدرب}}
\textbf{\ar{تدرب}} — \emph{tadarraba} — \textquotedblleft{}to practise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تدرب} \ar{الفريق} \ar{في} \ar{الملعب} \ar{كل} \ar{مساء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tadarraba al-farīq fī al-malʿab kull masāʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The team practised at the stadium every evening.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتدرب}, \emph{yatadarrab}.

It takes \ar{على} for the skill: \ar{تدرب} \ar{على} \ar{السباحة}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تدرب}} (\emph{tadarraba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-r-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to be used to, to be practised in\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form V tadarraba is to get oneself trained.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 512–519 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R519-review-512-519}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for recovery and convalescence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item recovery, convalescence, to recover, good health, to be in pain
  \item diabetes, asthma, a disability, to grow weak, to bleed
  \item insomnia, exhaustion, to wear out, to yawn, to doze off
  \item to snore, to relax, to lie down, to get up, fainting
  \item to stretch out, to bend down, to tremble, to have a cough, a sprain
  \item to smoke tobacco, to crave, to become addicted, to get hungry, to be full
  \item a profession, a secretary, a vet, an adviser, to aspire
  \item a CV, to volunteer, to donate, a trainee, to practise
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Recovery? (\textbf{\ar{شفاء}}, \emph{shifāʾ}.) Convalescence? (\textbf{\ar{نقاهة}}, \emph{naqāha}.) To recover? (\textbf{\ar{تعافى}}, \emph{taʿāfā}.) Good health? (\textbf{\ar{عافية}}, \emph{ʿāfiya}.) To be in pain? (\textbf{\ar{تألم}}, \emph{taʾallama}.) Diabetes? (\textbf{\ar{سكري}}, \emph{sukkarī}.) Asthma? (\textbf{\ar{ربو}}, \emph{rabw}.) A disability? (\textbf{\ar{إعاقة}}, \emph{iʿāqa}.) To grow weak? (\textbf{\ar{ضعف}}, \emph{ḍaʿufa}.) To bleed? (\textbf{\ar{نزف}}, \emph{nazafa}.) Insomnia? (\textbf{\ar{أرق}}, \emph{araq}.) Exhaustion? (\textbf{\ar{إرهاق}}, \emph{irhāq}.) To wear out? (\textbf{\ar{أرهق}}, \emph{arhaqa}.) To yawn? (\textbf{\ar{تثاءب}}, \emph{tathāʾaba}.) To doze off? (\textbf{\ar{غفا}}, \emph{ghafā}.) To snore? (\textbf{\ar{شخر}}, \emph{shakhara}.) To relax? (\textbf{\ar{استرخى}}, \emph{istarkhā}.) To lie down? (\textbf{\ar{استلقى}}, \emph{istalqā}.) To get up? (\textbf{\ar{نهض}}, \emph{nahaḍa}.) Fainting? (\textbf{\ar{إغماء}}, \emph{ighmāʾ}.) To stretch out? (\textbf{\ar{تمدد}}, \emph{tamaddada}.) To bend down? (\textbf{\ar{انحنى}}, \emph{inḥanā}.) To tremble? (\textbf{\ar{ارتجف}}, \emph{irtajafa}.) To have a cough? (\textbf{\ar{سعل}}, \emph{saʿala}.) A sprain? (\textbf{\ar{التواء}}, \emph{iltiwāʾ}.) To smoke tobacco? (\textbf{\ar{دخن}}, \emph{dakhkhana}.) To crave? (\textbf{\ar{اشتهى}}, \emph{ishtahā}.) To become addicted? (\textbf{\ar{أدمن}}, \emph{admana}.) To get hungry? (\textbf{\ar{جاع}}, \emph{jāʿa}.) To be full? (\textbf{\ar{شبع}}, \emph{shabiʿa}.) A profession? (\textbf{\ar{مهنة}}, \emph{mihna}.) A secretary? (\textbf{\ar{سكرتير}}, \emph{sikritīr}.) A vet? (\textbf{\ar{بيطري}}, \emph{bayṭarī}.) An adviser? (\textbf{\ar{مستشار}}, \emph{mustashār}.) To aspire? (\textbf{\ar{طمح}}, \emph{ṭamaḥa}.) A CV? (\textbf{\ar{سيرة} \ar{ذاتية}}, \emph{sīra dhātiyya}.) To volunteer? (\textbf{\ar{تطوع}}, \emph{taṭawwaʿa}.) To donate? (\textbf{\ar{تبرع}}, \emph{tabarraʿa}.) A trainee? (\textbf{\ar{متدرب}}, \emph{mutadarrib}.) To practise? (\textbf{\ar{تدرب}}, \emph{tadarraba}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
